dedupe_keys.name: preference based multi objective optimization for synchromodal transport using adaptive large neighborhood search

description: Zhang, Yimeng and colleagues publish this resource through the source community. The optimisation model formulates container transport as pickup and delivery with transshipment. Weight intervals represent decision-maker preferences for cost, time and emissions. Adaptive large-neighbourhood search produces a Pareto frontier, while four synchronisation cases examine how outgoing vehicles respond to incoming schedule changes. Coverage is designed Rhine-Alpine corridor case studies. Preferred nondominated solutions are reported; the record does not claim global optimality or that the tested policies were adopted by transport operators. Zenodo supplies the descriptive publication with open access under cc-by-4.0. The publication does not establish public access to an implementation or its separate licence. A limitation is that complete implementation or measurement settings cannot be reconstructed from descriptive metadata alone. Related experimental components and publications retain their distinct roles; separate deposits are not assumed to provide independent observations.
